intro:
You're a business owner still filming every video yourself? AI can do that for you. The reel that sent you here was not filmed. I gave Claude three photos of my face and a voice memo, and about an hour later I had a 55-second vertical video of me talking, with captions, graphics and music.

This guide is the exact setup I used, including the two things that went wrong and how I fixed each one with a single sentence. One thing to know up front: this kit remakes one specific reel, a promo for Higgsfield's Shorts Studio. The script, captions and music come with it. They aren't yours or mine. You get the same video with your face and your voice in it. It's the fastest way to see what this technology does with you on screen before you build your own.

free.title: Step 1: What you need (and what it costs)
free.body:
1. Claude for desktop, on a paid plan. The phone app and the website won't run this.
  2. A Higgsfield account with credits. Higgsfield is the video tool Claude drives. Their page says one reel uses about 2,600 credits. Mine used about 3,250, because I had Claude redo two pieces. Plan for 3,500 so you don't stall halfway.
  3. Three photos and one voice memo. Your phone is enough.
  4. About an hour. You do five minutes of work. The rest is waiting while the videos generate.

Create your Higgsfield account →

That's my partner link. If you sign up through it I may earn a commission, at no extra cost to you.

Buy the credits before you start, and check that your balance went up on the same Higgsfield login you connect to Claude. I bought mine on one login and Claude was looking at another, and it cost me twenty minutes.

free.title: Step 2: Take three photos
free.body:
Front, left side, right side. Same spot, same clothes, one after the other.

  • Face big and sharp, with good light coming from the front. A window in front of you works.
  • Waist-up if you can. What you wear in the photos is what you wear in the video.
  • No filters, no beauty mode, no sunglasses, nobody else in the frame.
  • Take off anything you don't want in the video. I left bright orange earbuds in, and they're in every shot of my reel.

free.title: Step 3: Record your voice (29 seconds or less)
free.body:
Use the voice memo app on your phone. Quiet room, phone close to your mouth, no music. Talk the way you normally talk. Keep it between 10 and 29 seconds: longer than 29 and it won't be accepted.

Read this out loudHi, this is my voice for the video. I usually record short clips about the tools I use every day, and I like to keep them simple and honest. Today I want to show you something that saved me hours of editing this week. Let me walk you through it step by step, so you can try it yourself right after watching.

My memo ran 54 seconds, so Claude trimmed it to the cleanest 29. Save yourself the step and stop at 29.

free.title: Step 4: Get the skill
free.body:
A skill is a small folder of instructions that teaches Claude one job. This is the same file I used. Download it here:

Download the reel skill (40 MB) →

Leave the file zipped. You don't need to open it.

free.title: Step 5: Set up Claude (once)
free.body:
1. Open Claude for desktop and go to Settings, then Capabilities. Turn on Code execution and file creation, and turn on Skills.
  2. Still in Capabilities, open Skills, choose Upload skill, and pick the zip you downloaded.
  3. Go to Settings, then Connectors. Turn on Higgsfield and sign in with the account that has your credits.

You only do this once. Next time you skip straight to Step 6.

free.title: Step 6: Send it to Claude
free.body:
Start a new chat. Attach your three photos and your voice memo, then send this:

Copy this in (with the 3 photos and the voice memo attached)Study the reels-revoice-higgsfield skill. I attached everything you need from me: three photos (front, left side, right side) and my voice. Tell me the credit estimate and my balance, then go.

Claude checks your balance, tells you the cost, and starts. Here's what it does while you wait:

  1. Makes the original presenter say the script in your voice, with the lips matched.
  2. Replaces him with you, using your three photos. His gestures stay. The face, hair and clothes become yours.
  3. Puts your face on the small editing screens that pop up in the video.
  4. Adds the captions, graphics and music, timed to your words.

Midway through, Claude will show you clips of a stranger talking in your voice. That's normal. It's the step before your face goes in.

free.title: Step 7: Check it, then fix one thing at a time
free.body:
When Claude sends the finished reel, watch it twice. Look for three things:

  • It's your face in every shot, including the close-ups from the side.
  • The captions match what you're saying.
  • No stray text or fake app windows that don't belong.

If something's off, ask for one small fix at a time. Claude redoes only that piece, which costs far fewer credits than starting over. These are the two I needed:

If one shot doesn't look like youFrom [0:21 to 0:23] it doesn't look like me. Redo only that shot and put it back into the video.
If extra text or a fake window shows upThere is extra text in the video around [0:20] that shouldn't be there. Redo that part without it.

Other fixes that work the same way: "The captions don't match my voice, please fix it." "The small editing screen still shows someone else, fix it."

Listen to the brand names too. Mine says "Higgsfield" a little strangely. A voice redo costs about 1,000 credits per half of the video, so decide if it bothers you enough.

free.title: Step 8: Post it
free.body:
1. Download the video from the link Claude gives you.
  2. When you upload, turn on the AI-generated label. Instagram, TikTok and YouTube all ask for it on realistic AI video of a person, and it's you, so own it. "I didn't film this" is the hook anyway.
  3. Write your own caption. Say what it is: you, made from three photos and a voice memo.

Remember what this reel is: someone else's script with you in it. Post it as a demo of what AI can do with your face and voice. For videos about your own business, in your own words, you need your own format. That's what I build next.
